verdicts.claim: A checkpoint moves transactions from the WAL file back into the main database file; by default SQLite runs one automatically when the WAL
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: 'SQLite does a checkpoint automatically when the WAL file reaches a threshold size of 1000 pages'; pragma.html: default page size 4096 since 3.12.0 (=~4 MB)

verdicts.claim: PASSIVE checkpoints as many frames as possible without waiting for readers or writers and never invokes the busy handler
verdicts.evidence: c3ref: 'The busy-handler callback is never invoked in the SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_PASSIVE mode... might leave the checkpoint unfinished if there are concurrent readers or writers'

verdicts.claim: FULL takes the writer lock and waits (via the busy handler) until there is no writer and all readers are on the latest snapshot; RESTART
verdicts.evidence: c3ref defines FULL/RESTART/TRUNCATE ('truncates the log file to zero bytes') and NOOP ('always checkpoints zero frames') as stated

verdicts.claim: PRAGMA wal_autocheckpoint=N (wrapper for sqlite3_wal_autocheckpoint) sets the auto-checkpoint threshold in pages; ... all automatic checkpoints are PASSIVE
verdicts.evidence: pragma.html: 'wrapper around the sqlite3_wal_autocheckpoint() C interface. All automatic checkpoints are PASSIVE... interval of 1000 or SQLITE_DEFAULT_WAL_AUTOCHECKPOINT'

verdicts.claim: PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(MODE) returns one row (busy, log, checkpointed): busy=1 means a FULL/RESTART/TRUNCATE checkpoint was blocked
verdicts.evidence: pragma.html: 'returns a single row with three integer columns. The first column is usually 0 but will be 1 if a RESTART or FULL or TRUNCATE checkpoint was blocked'

verdicts.claim: Litestream disables application auto-checkpoints (recommends PRAGMA wal_autocheckpoint = 0) ... applications should set busy_timeout (5000 ms suggested)
verdicts.evidence: tips: 'recommended to run your application with autocheckpointing disabled... PRAGMA wal_autocheckpoint = 0;' and 'PRAGMA busy_timeout = 5000;'

verdicts.claim: Checkpoints issue fsyncs and are slower than write transactions; with synchronous=NORMAL they are the only syncing operation, so moving
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: 'with PRAGMA synchronous set to NORMAL, the checkpoint is the only operation to issue an I/O barrier or sync operation'; checkpoints 'slower than write transactions'

verdicts.claim: A checkpoint cannot copy frames beyond the snapshot of the oldest active read transaction, so a long-running reader, or a continuous stream
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: 'if a database has many concurrent overlapping readers and there is always at least one active reader... the WAL file will grow without bound'

verdicts.claim: Every checkpoint takes an exclusive checkpoint lock; if another connection is already checkpointing, the call returns SQLITE_BUSY immediately
verdicts.evidence: c3ref: 'All calls obtain an exclusive "checkpoint" lock... SQLITE_BUSY is returned. Even if there is a busy-handler configured, it will not be invoked'; degrade-to-PASSIVE also stated

verdicts.claim: The WAL-reset bug ... affects 3.7.0 through 3.51.2 and is fixed in 3.51.3 (2026-03-13), with backports to 3.44.6 and 3.50.7. The 3.52.0 release
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: 'present in all version of SQLite from 3.7.0 (2010-07-21) through 3.51.2... fixed in version 3.51.3 (2026-03-13)... Backports... 3.44.6 and 3.50.7'. The 3.52.0-withdrawn clause is NOT in either cited source; sqlite.org/news (via WebSearch) says 3.52.0 was withdrawn.
